name: bugbear
skin_color: Mustard yellow to deep russet hide
special_features: Coarse fur, unnaturally long limbs, predatory features
lore:
To the uninitiated, the bugbear is a mere brute; to the survivor, it is a ghost clad in coarse fur. Standing nearly seven feet tall, these hulking goblinoids possess unnaturally long limbs and a muscular build that belies their uncanny silence. Their hides, ranging from mustard yellow to deep russet, are matted with thick hair, and their faces bear the flattened features of a predator designed for the dark. Despite their mass, they move with the grace of a stalking cat.

Their origins are steeped in the iron will of the conqueror-god Maglubiyet, though older myths whisper of Hruggek, the god of ambush. While kin to the nimble goblin and the disciplined hobgoblin, the bugbear was forged for a singular purpose: terror. Legends suggest they were birthed from the shadows of ancient forests to serve as the vanguard of goblinoid hosts, though most have since slipped into a more primal, solitary existence.

Culturally, bugbears are governed by a lethargic ruthlessness. They are the quintessential ambush predators, preferring to spend days in slumber only to erupt into a whirlwind of violence when prey wanders near. They do not build cities; they occupy the ruins of others or nest in damp caverns. Within their loose social circles, might is the only law. They bully their smaller cousins into servitude, viewing honest labor as a plight for the weak. To a bugbear, the highest virtue is the "quiet kill"—the ability to fell a foe before a single scream can escape. If you hear the snap of a twig in the deep woods, do not turn; run. For if a bugbear wishes to be seen, it is already too late.
